summary: Lewis Robert Stacy (1787–1848) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held a post at the East India Company in 1804 and served as a Lieutenant-Colonel in the Bengal Army from circa 1804 to 1848.

Lewis Sydney Stewart O'Malley (1874–1941) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned a B.A. from Hertford College, Oxford (circa 1893–1897) and served as a Magistrate and Collector in the Indian Civil Service (1898–1924).

id: P:Lha Zang Lama Rigdzin Gar Gyi Wangchuk
summary: Lha Zang Lama Rigdzin Gar Gyi Wangchuk studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Lhagpa Phuntshogs is a Tibetologist who founded the STTAR series. He served as president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (1983–1991), secretary-general of the Research Association for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (1991–2000), and Director General of the China Tibetology Research Center (2000).

Working in Tibetology and linguistics, Lhakpa Tsering has served as a Professor at Tibet University and, as attested in 2026, as Assistant Professor of Tibetan Language and Literature at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Li-Juan Su works in Buddhist studies. She earned a master's degree from National Taiwan Normal University and has been a PhD student at National Chengchi University, where she held a PhD student post in 2024.

Li-ching Chang (1936–2010) was a sinologist and linguist who taught Mandarin Chinese at the University of Washington, Tunghai University, Bryn Mawr College, Harvard University, Swarthmore College, and the University of Pennsylvania (circa 1978–2004).
Liang Cai is a scholar in sinology, history, and archaeology. She studied under Daniel Boucher and held an appointment as a junior scholar at the University of Arkansas, attested in 2014.
Indologist Libbie Mills earned her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson in 2011. She taught Sanskrit and Pali at the University of Toronto, attested in 2020.

Lidia Wojtczak is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She served as Lecturer in Sanskrit at SOAS University of London (2015–2024) and became Associate Instructional Professor in Sanskrit at the University of Chicago in 2024.
Lifei Pan, a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology, studied at Ghent University and Sichuan University, where he held a postdoctoral post in 2021.
Lili Zheng works in Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi, attested in 2011.

Lilian Silburn (1908–1993) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She studied under Paul Masson-Oursel, Louis Renou, and Swami Lakshman Joo, and held posts at the CNRS (circa 1945–1974; boursière 1950–1970).

Lilias Homburger (1880–1969) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Antoine Meillet (circa 1906–1913). She taught at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales and served as directeur d’études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (circa 1930–1951).

Lilla Russell-Smith works in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Anna Eörsi and Pál Miklós, and earned a PhD from SOAS University of London.

Lily de Silva worked in Indology and Buddhist studies, having studied under M. Sri Rammandala and traditional teacher Julius Berugoda. She held posts at the University of Ceylon (attested 1970) and the University of Peradeniya (attested 2008).

Limei Chi works in Buddhist studies and sinology and studied under Jinhua Chen. As attested in 2026, she holds posts on the faculty at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and as Professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Lin He (1902–1992) was a philosopher who studied at Tsinghua University (National Tsing Hua University) from circa 1919 to 1926. He later held a post at National Tsing Hua University from circa 1931 to 1948.
Lin Heng specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at Silpakorn University under the supervision of Chainarong Klinnoi, attested in 2015.
Lin Li is a scholar in computational linguistics who has held posts at Utrecht University and Qinghai Normal University.
